claims.statement: Any nonnegative row detector equal to one on every failed row excludes failures when its total mass is below one.
The frozen weighted occupancy detector equals one on a zero row and is nonnegative under nonnegative weights.
Uniform INT-AOD is the expected number of uncovered rows under independent candidate-offset sampling with probability q_X.
Sampling exactly K of M candidate offsets misses a row with Z successful offsets with probability binom(M-Z,K)/binom(M,K).
The exact without-replacement analogue of the constant-q detector has degree Theta(M_X)=Theta(X^2/log X).
A convergent connected expansion whose first cumulant exceeds the absolute connected remainder by more than log N implies INT-AOD.
Disconnected prime-tuple contributions can be cancelled before estimating the aggregate connected remainder.
A precisely parameterized row-uniform growing-tuple Hardy-Littlewood hypothesis implies INT-AOD or INT-CCB.
A smallest explicit row-uniform parity-breaking bilinear estimate implies INT-AOD.
Finite primorial panels and adversarial incidence matrices may falsify methods but cannot prove asymptotic Fortune statements.
